question: What claim about agency is at stake in holding that the yoginī named Will, by supreme will, is set to the end of Māyā by the siddhas?
premises: A yoginī named Icchā is in view.
The siddhas act in relation to her up to the end of Māyā.
That action occurs by supreme will.
inference: By supreme will, the siddhas direct the yoginī Icchā to the limit of Māyā.
uncertainties: The precise function assigned to her at the end of Māyā is not stated here.
plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by supreme will, is placed by the siddhas up to the end of Māyā.
